qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: High customer switching costs and workflow lock-in across civil engineering, BIM structural design (Tekla), and construction project management. Tangible ROIC exceeds 80%, though aggressive serial M&A keeps 10-year median GAAP ROIC suppressed at ~7.4%.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). Enterprise software and capital goods baseline (Tier 3, 10-15Y) receives substantial haircuts due to cyclicality in construction and freight transportation end-markets, ongoing terminal disruption risks from generative AI and CAD automation on seat-based modeling tools, and an aggressive serial M&A roll-up strategy that dilutes capital efficiency (10Y median GAAP ROIC 7.4%, FCF conversion 55.7%) and led to substantial goodwill accumulation and subsequent impairments.
qualitative.evidence: Trimble exhibits a multi-decade public operating history connecting physical and digital workflows across AECO (Architecture, Engineering, Construction, and Owners), Geospatial, and Transportation & Logistics. While tangible ROIC is high due to low physical asset intensity, GAAP ROIC has persistently tracked below hurdles at a 5-year median of 7.37% (ranging from 5.1% to 10.1% across 2016-2025) and multi-year Owner FCF conversion is weak at 55.7%, weighed down by continuous M&A integration costs and capitalized intangibles ($6.16B goodwill and intangibles vs $5.84B equity in FY2025). The $2.1B debt-financed acquisition of Transporeon in 2023 pushed leverage above 3.5x and subsequently faced severe freight market headwinds leading to a $562M segment goodwill impairment. Furthermore, generative AI tools and spatial computing automation threaten seat-based engineering, CAD drafting (Tekla, SketchUp), and estimation workflows, preventing the business from achieving secular resilience required for a 15+ year competitive advantage period.
